title: ☁️ upload backup
body:
# 🧭 Steps

1. **Export** — build/refresh `~/backup/git-tags/`:
   - **Public repos** — export latest tag as **raw zip** into each folder: `browser-extensions/`, `browser-games/`, `interview/`, `radar-alerts/`.
   - **Private wiki** — export as encrypted **`private.zip`** only (never raw tree).
   - Split any file **> 4 GB** with `zip -s 4g` (FAT32 cap).
2. Check every file is ≤ 4 GB before copy.
3. **USB 1** — copy full tree; verify file count and size; label with pass date.
4. **USB 2** — repeat copy (second FAT32 mirror).
5. **iCloud Drive** — sync into `backup/git-tags/`.
6. **OneDrive** — sync under Documents backup folder.
7. **Proton Drive** — sync backup folder.
8. **Google Drive** — sync shared backup folder.
9. Wait for cloud uploads idle; eject USB safely.

Drive credentials live in the private providers file.

## 📁 Backup rules

- **Fire and forget** — drives are best-effort: if you can access the data, great — but it may be deleted due to lack of usage. Always keep the USB pendrive as the reliable copy; drives are extra copies, not guarantees.
- **Recommended flow** — build the raw backup on the USB pendrive first, then upload to all online drives in a row from there.
- **Organization** — mirror the folder structure; one `.zip` per tag.
- **Naming** — `reponame_yyyy-mm-dd_x.y.z.zip` (e.g. `records_2026-08-04_1.2.0.zip`).
- **Repo sizes:**

<!-- begin table -->
| Repo | Per-tag size |
|---|---|
| public/* (all) | ~1 MB (max 8 MB) |
| private/records | ~40 MB |
<!-- end table -->

## 🗂️ Canonical tree

```bash
~/backup/git-tags/
├── browser-extensions/
├── browser-games/
├── control-plane/
├── interview/
├── radar-alerts/
├── private.zip
├── template/
└── yugioh/
```

## 💾 Media

2× USB pendrives, **FAT32**, cross-OS. Hard limit **4 GB per file**.

## ✅ Done when

- Local tree has all five entries (4 public folders + encrypted `private.zip`)
- Both FAT32 USB sticks updated and date-labeled
- All four cloud destinations show the same recent sync
- No file on any destination exceeds 4 GB
